obligation: CPNI breach notice to law enforcement (current rule)
trigger: Reasonable determination that a person, without or exceeding authorization, intentionally gained access to, used, or disclosed CPNI (64.2011(e)); in runbook 1, confirmed theft of call detail records
deadline: As soon as practicable and no later than 7 business days after reasonable determination (internal target: 2 business days)
notify: USSS and FBI electronically through the FCC central reporting facility (link at fcc.gov/eb/cpni)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - telecommunications carrier and interconnected VoIP provider (64.2003(o)); no size exemption
clock_starts: Reasonable determination of the breach (date and basis recorded in the incident log)
owner: Vice President of Regulatory Affairs with counsel

obligation: CPNI breach: hold on customer and public notice
trigger: Law enforcement notice filed
deadline: No customer or public disclosure until 7 full business days after the USSS/FBI notice, notwithstanding contrary state law. Earlier notice only if the carrier flags an extraordinarily urgent need and consults the investigating agency; the agency may direct a delay of up to 30 days, extendable
notify: Hold; log any agency direction (the agency logs it on the reporting facility)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
clock_starts: Filing of the law enforcement notice
owner: Chief Operating Officer; Director of Customer Operations (holding scripts)

obligation: CPNI breach notice to customers (current rule)
trigger: Law enforcement notice process complete
deadline: After the 7-full-business-day hold ends (or as the agency directs); the current rule sets no further outer deadline, so plan to the state-law clocks below
notify: Each customer whose CPNI was breached; enterprise and government accounts through their account representatives
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
owner: Vice President of Regulatory Affairs with counsel

trigger: Any breach discovered
deadline: Record kept for at least 2 years: dates of discovery and notice, description of the CPNI, circumstances
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: CPNI and covered data breach notice (2023 amendments; NOT yet effective)
citation: 47 CFR 64.2011 as amended by FCC 23-111 (89 FR 9968); upheld in Ohio Telecom Ass'n v. FCC (6th Cir. 2025-08-13)
trigger: Would cover inadvertent as well as intentional access, and customer PII as well as CPNI
deadline: Would require FCC, USSS, and FBI notice within 7 business days; customer notice without unreasonable delay and within 30 days after reasonable determination; breaches under 500 customers with no reasonably likely harm reported in an annual summary
applies_at_this_tier: No - amendments to 64.2011 remain delayed indefinitely; no FCC effective-date notice in the Federal Register through 2026-10-05; eCFR (2026-09-23) shows the prior text. Recheck at every incident

trigger: Opt-out mechanisms do not work properly to a degree that customers' inability to opt out is more than an anomaly (for example, a BSS outage that corrupts approval flags)
deadline: Written notice (letter) within 5 business days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

trigger: Any compromise of a lawful interception or of call-identifying information to unauthorized persons, or any unlawful electronic surveillance on company premises
deadline: Within a reasonable time upon discovery
notify: Affected law enforcement agencies (through the CALEA TTP and the agency contacts in the SSI appendix)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if SYS-10 or intercept records are reached or cannot be ruled out
owner: Vice President of Network Operations (CALEA senior officer)

trigger: Outage that potentially affects a 911 special facility, including one caused by containment actions (for example, isolating an SBC or a central office)
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 minutes after discovery, by telephone and in writing electronically; first follow-up no later than 2 hours after initial contact, then as new material information is available
notify: Designated outage contacts at each affected PSAP (contacts confirmed annually, 4.9(h)(1))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - wireline, interconnected VoIP, and covered 911 service provider

trigger: Outage that potentially affects a 988 special facility
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 minutes after discovery; first follow-up no later than 2 hours after initial contact
notify: Designated contacts at the affected 988 special facility
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 988 calls are affected

trigger: Wireline outage of at least 30 minutes that potentially affects 900,000 user minutes, 667 OC3 minutes, special offices and facilities, or a 911 or 988 special facility
deadline: Notification within 120 minutes of discovery; Initial Communications Outage Report within 72 hours; Final Communications Outage Report within 30 days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - thresholds are outage-based, not size-based
owner: NOC Director; Vice President of Network Operations approves

obligation: FCC outage report (interconnected VoIP, including hosted voice)
trigger: VoIP outage of at least 30 minutes that potentially affects a 911 or 988 special facility; or 900,000 user minutes with complete loss of service; or special offices and facilities
deadline: Notification within 240 minutes (911 or 988 facility affected) or 24 hours (other triggers); Final Communications Outage Report within 30 days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 54,500 VoIP lines including 14,200 hosted voice seats

trigger: FCC activates DIRS for the service area (for example, a hurricane during the incident)
deadline: Daily infrastructure status reports from activation until deactivation; timely DIRS reporting can replace NORS for outages in the activated area
applies_at_this_tier: Yes when activated

trigger: Traceback request from the FCC, law enforcement, or the industry traceback consortium (for example, calls spoofed through a compromised hosted voice tenant)
deadline: Within 24 hours of the request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voice service provider

citation: 47 CFR 9.20(a)(2)(ii) as amended by FCC 26-39 (91 FR 42794)
trigger: Material change to networks, facilities, operations, or reliability practices that makes a previous certification inaccurate (for example, loss of diversity after an attack)
deadline: Within 90 days of discovering the material change, unless remedied within that period
applies_at_this_tier: Not yet - initial certifications are due 18 months after a compliance-date notice not yet published as of 2026-10-05; keep records now

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents. Personal information includes name plus SSN, government ID number, financial account with access code, medical or health insurance data, biometric data, or geolocation; or a user name or email with a password or security question and answer. Call detail alone may not qualify; counsel decides
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred (a 15-day extension is available for good cause, for this notice only). Notice under the primary or functional federal regulator's rules is deemed compliant if a copy is timely provided to the Department of Legal Affairs; counsel decides whether FCC CPNI notice qualifies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if Florida-defined personal information is involved (for example, portal credentials, SSN digits)
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (no extension for this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500+ Florida residents' personal information

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice (inbound from vendors)
trigger: A vendor that maintains or processes personal information for the company (BSS, CCaaS, chatbot, overflow call center, bill print) has a breach
deadline: Vendor must notify the company within 10 days of determination
notify: The company (Vice President of Regulatory Affairs)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in vendor contracts (POAM-015)

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents of other states (about 8% of residential accounts belong to seasonal residents)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Always check. Apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties
owner: General Counsel; Chief Executive Officer decides

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident / ransom payment reports (pending final rule)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Statute: 72 hours (covered incident); 24 hours (ransom payment) - not yet effective
applies_at_this_tier: No - no final rule published as of 2026-10-05. Voluntary report to CISA and FBI on day 0-2 instead
clock_starts: Would be reasonable belief of a covered incident

trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at a public registrant
deadline: 4 business days after materiality determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - privately held (PE-backed); lenders and the sponsor are notified under contract instead

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal prime contracts or subcontracts

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal prime contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Business Services and enterprise customer contract notice
citation: Customer contracts (Business Services; 320 enterprise and government accounts with CPNI terms)
trigger: Security incident affecting the customer's data or services, or an outage under the SLA
deadline: Per contract (Business Services contracts: 24 hours for confirmed security incidents); customer notice of a CPNI breach still waits for the 64.2011(b) hold unless the investigating agency agrees
notify: Customer contract contacts through the account representatives
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not regulatory

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not regulatory

citation: Credit agreement and sponsor reporting terms (contract)
trigger: Severity 1 incident or material outage
deadline: Per credit agreement (prompt notice of material events)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual
